classification.classification_note: ASan reports `use-after-poison` because AFL++ user-poisons bytes immediately after the actual input length. Source review shows the underlying defect is an unbounded C-string parse of a non-NUL-terminated 23-byte buffer, not a free-after-use lifetime bug.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42516681 (gpsd): Use-after-poison READ 1 found by fuzz target FuzzJson [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42516681
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged `poc` is the 23-byte ASCII prefix `{"class":"ERROR","messa` with no trailing NUL. In the staged untracked harness `fuzzer/FuzzJson.c`, that raw file buffer passes the size guard and is cast directly to `char *` for `libgps_json_unpack((char *)Data, &gpsdata, NULL)`. `libgps_json_unpack()` searches `buf` with `strstr()` and finds `"class":` at `buf + 1`; the bytes at that pointer satisfy `str_starts_with(classtag, "\"class\":\"ERROR\"")`, so the ERROR arm calls `json_error_read()`. `json_error_read()` sends the same buffer to `json_read_object()`, and `json_internal_read_object()` consumes the valid prefix `{"class":"ERROR",` before treating the quote at byte 17 as the start of the next attribute name. Only the five bytes `messa` remain, so the parser stays in `in_attr` state with no closing quote and, more importantly, no terminating `\0` inside the 23-byte witness. Its main loop at `libgps/json.c:280` stops only on `*cp == '\0'`, not on the actual input length, so when `cp` advances to offset 23 the loop condition dereferences the first AFL++-poisoned byte immediately past the witness. Stage 01's ASan trace records `use-after-poison READ of size 1` at `json_internal_read_object` line 280. The metadata `fix_commit` and staged `patch.diff` only modify `safe_atof()` and tests, so they do not explain or resolve this reproduced path.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the raw fuzz bytes and materializes a pointer to the JSON class tag used for parser dispatch.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 23 bytes: `7b 22 63 6c 61 73 73 22 3a 22 45 52 52 4f 52 22 2c 22 6d 65 73 73 61`, i.e. the unterminated ASCII prefix `{"class":"ERROR","messa`. This `strstr()` finds `"class":` at `buf + 1`, proving the witness is admitted to class-based dispatch.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The generic JSON object parser treats `cp` as a NUL-terminated C string and stops only when `*cp == '\0'`; it has no caller-supplied length or end pointer limiting reads to the 23-byte witness.
root_cause.note: By the time this loop reevaluates on the witness, the parser has already consumed `{"class":"ERROR",` and started the next attribute name from the truncated fragment `messa`, so no in-bounds terminator exists before the poison boundary. The staged metadata fix commit and `patch.diff` do not modify this path, and no matching fix was identified in the prepared local gpsd history.

sink.description: ASan sink. When the loop condition is reevaluated after the parser advances past all 23 addressable bytes, dereferencing `*cp` reads the first user-poisoned byte immediately after the fuzz input.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `libgps/json.c:280:12` with stack `json_internal_read_object -> json_error_read -> libgps_json_unpack -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; the poisoned address is 23 bytes inside the 1 MiB AFL++ input region.

tainted_value_origin.description: The staged harness forwards the fuzz bytes directly as a `char *` JSON buffer with no appended NUL terminator or length argument.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved `poc` length is exactly 23 bytes, and the ASan shadow `00 00 07 f7 ...` in `sanitizer_trace.txt` shows bytes after offset 23 are user-poisoned rather than part of the input.

parser_admitted.description: The bytes starting at `classtag` exactly match the prefix `"class":"ERROR"`, so the ERROR parser arm is selected before the input ends.

evidence_limitations: The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` only modify `libgps/gpsutils.c` and `tests/test_json.c`; they do not touch `libgps/json.c`, `libgps/libgps_json.c`, or the staged `fuzzer/FuzzJson.c` harness that participates in the reproduced crash path.

The staged `fuzzer/FuzzJson.c` file is untracked in the prepared gpsd checkout, so the reproduced crash depends on a harness that is present in the Stage 01 workspace but not in local gpsd git history.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact staged witness is the 23-byte raw buffer `{"class":"ERROR","messa`; this call passes those bytes as `char *` with no trailing NUL and no separate length argument to the library JSON decoder. The size guard at lines 33-35 is satisfied because `23` is between `kMinInputLength` and `kMaxInputLength`.

Source. The library consumes the raw buffer as a C string and materializes `classtag` by searching for `"class":`; on the witness, the search succeeds at `buf + 1` before any poisoned byte is touched.

The dispatch predicate is satisfied because bytes 1-15 of the witness are exactly `"class":"ERROR"`. That control decision selects the `ERROR` decoder and makes the generic object parser reachable on the same raw buffer.

The `ERROR` decoder forwards the same non-NUL-terminated buffer into `json_read_object()` with the `class` and `message` attribute table. No length is added or checked before the generic parser starts scanning `buf`.

After the parser has already consumed the valid prefix `{"class":"ERROR",`, it sees the quote before the remaining bytes `messa` and starts a second attribute name. `state` becomes `in_attr` and `pattr` begins filling `attrbuf`, but the 23-byte witness never supplies the closing quote or any in-bounds `\0` terminator for that attribute.

Root cause. The main object-parser loop uses only `*cp != '\0'` as its stop condition. Because step 1 supplied a raw 23-byte buffer and step 5 started an attribute that is truncated at `messa`, this loop has no length-bound stop condition before the poison fence.

Sink. After the parser copies the five available attribute-name bytes `messa`, `cp` advances to offset 23. Reevaluating the same loop condition dereferences `*cp` at that offset and reads the first user-poisoned byte immediately beyond the witness, which is the exact `READ of size 1` reported by ASan.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: n/a: the poisoned byte is the end-of-input fence inside the AFL++ buffer, so the malloc site in `ExecuteFilesOnyByOne` is not the missing bound.

poc.trigger: Pass the exact 23-byte file `{"class":"ERROR","messa` to `FuzzJson`; the prefix is enough to select `json_error_read()`, and because the file ends inside the next attribute name with no trailing NUL, `json_internal_read_object()` scans one byte past the end of the input and hits the fuzzer-poisoned fence.

format.name: raw JSON prefix bytes
format.contract: Exact 23-byte ASCII prefix `{"class":"ERROR","messa` with no trailing NUL byte. The trigger semantics rely on both facts: the buffer must contain the full `"class":"ERROR"` dispatch prefix, and it must end immediately after the five-byte fragment `messa` so the parser remains inside an unterminated attribute name when it reaches byte 23.
